C3. Node QC proves operation logic but not that a browser can run it, so the operations are now bundled and executed inside Chromium and WebKit against the same output contract, and the image editor and PDF page tools are driven through their real UI. All 615 operations and all 13 UI destinations pass in both engines: no tool needed removing. Three real problems were found and fixed: the e2e suite had been attaching to another project's dev server on port 3000, so all 628 route smoke tests were passing against an unrelated app (now its own port, production build, plus a global setup that refuses a foreign server); WebKit returns a PNG for a canvas WebP request, which the image editor and optimizer treated as failure, leaving both dead on that engine at their default WebP setting (they now keep the produced blob, name the file for its real format and show it on the receipt); and two legacy specs fed the AI background remover a flat single-colour square with no subject, which the model correctly refused.

Compress PDF is the most-searched PDF tool and the one competitors gate hardest; it now runs with no upload at /pdf/compress. A lossless pass rewrites with object streams and can clear document metadata; an image pass re-encodes embedded JPEGs and downsamples oversized ones. Only images that can be rewritten without changing how the page renders are touched (single DCTDecode filter, 8 bpc, DeviceRGB or DeviceGray, no custom decode array); CMYK, indexed and ICC images are left alone. If the output is not smaller the original bytes are returned and the receipt says so. Figures are measured on a noise-heavy 3-page photo PDF, close to the worst case for any codec. The e2e specs save the real download and reopen it with pdf-lib rather than trusting the on-screen receipt. The /guides/pdf-compress-pdf guide pointed at a control the page tool never had and now points at the tool that runs it.

Filling and signing a PDF is the paid-tier feature at every competitor and the one people most often hand to a stranger's server. /pdf/sign now does it in the tab. inspectPdfForm reads the real AcroForm and reports each field's kind and the options a choice field accepts, so the UI cannot offer a value the file would reject. fillPdfForm writes the values, stamps an optional PNG signature and can flatten; placement converts the UI's top-left coordinates to the PDF's bottom-left origin against the real page height so the mark lands where it was dropped on any page size. Two limits are stated on the page rather than implied away: this draws a signature and does not certify one (no certificate, no audit trail), and drawing needs a pointer with no keyboard equivalent yet. The e2e specs save the real download and reopen it with pdf-lib to read back the written values, assert flattening actually removes the form, and cover a PDF with no fields at all. /guides/pdf-sign-pdf and /guides/pdf-fill-pdf-form pointed at a ?tool= control the page tool never had and now point at the tool that runs them. Committed, not deployed.

C5. The EXIF and metadata scrubber told every user that all EXIF, GPS locations, camera serials and thumbnail metadata had been completely stripped, and its notice advertised a 100% metadata-free image file. For WebP, HEIC, AVIF, TIFF and GIF it returned the input bytes unchanged while saying that. On a site whose whole pitch is privacy this is the claim that makes someone trust a file enough to send it to another person, so it was treated as the most serious class of untrue claim rather than a copy defect. Five faults were reproduced in the code before any edit. Format is now detected from magic bytes rather than the filename: JPEG and PNG are cleaned, and every other container is refused by name with no download produced, because this tool edits containers directly and has no decoder for the rest; a mixed batch cleans what it can and lists what it refused. APP2 (ICC) and APP14 (Adobe) are kept, since the old isMetadataMarker range dropped them along with the EXIF it was aiming at, shifting colour and potentially inverting CMYK JPEGs, which means the scrubber damaged the image it was asked to clean. Orientation lives inside the EXIF being removed, so when the source declares a rotation a minimal EXIF block carrying only the Orientation tag is re-emitted; without it phone photos turned sideways on download. The SOS branch copied to end of file, so trailers past EOI survived, which is exactly where motion-photo video and its location data sit; output is now truncated at the real end-of-image, found by scanning for FF D9 since entropy-coded data byte-stuffs FF as FF 00. The result reports per file exactly what was removed and what was kept, and states plainly when parsing stopped early and the remainder was copied unchanged rather than silently implying a clean pass. Pixels are never re-encoded. Two harnesses were themselves part of the bug: all-operations-qc.test.ts and e2e/operations-browser-harness.ts fed a .txt fixture to every file operation, so they asserted the scrubber succeeded on a text file, which is how the old code passed its own gates while being wrong; both now supply a real PNG. Pushed to main as f3eda07..6e1c263, fast-forward. Not deployed: main is release-verified and the production build is clean, but npm run deploy was refused by the session tool-permission layer, so the live site still runs dd046171 and neither this fix nor the Sign and fill fix is live.

Eleven /guides/ URLs in the sitemap returned 503 to every client, including Googlebot. wrangler tail gave outcome exceededCpu with 'Worker exceeded CPU time limit' and cpuTime 10, the free plan's 10ms cap. It was never the page code: the same build served all sampled failures locally at 200 in about 10ms, and a healthy guide renders in 5ms, so the failures were simply the pages costing roughly twice as much against a ceiling the cheaper ones cleared. The owner had upgraded to Workers Paid and KV writes resumed immediately because quota is account-level, which made the upgrade look fully applied while CPU limits stayed at free-tier values. CPU limits attach to the deployed Worker version, so redeploying the identical commit c97a470 with zero code or config changes was both the test and the fix: all 11 now return 200. Recorded for future reference: after any Cloudflare plan change, redeploy. Separately, the follow-up 629-URL re-warm reported 244 curl status-000 failures and a 127-second hang, which was NOT a site fault but this client tripping Cloudflare rate limiting: the failures clustered in time rather than by page, every affected URL returns 200 afterwards, tail recorded outcome ok with no exceptions, and a random 30-URL sample gave HIT=21 MISS=9 other=0. That is the same self-inflicted pattern as the 2026-09-16 incident, where an audit crawl produced the load event it then reported. Conclusion written to the board: do not bulk-warm this site; the cache fills on real traffic and stale-while-revalidate keeps entries usable.

Owner decision 13. engine/index.ts re-exports the tool logic that runs without React, Next/Vinext, app/, components/, workers/ or any network API, so the same code can later back a CLI or MCP server. boundary.test.ts walks the real import graph with the TypeScript parser (static, type-only, export-from, dynamic import expressions and types, require, triple-slash) and checks third-party packages by manifest and by scanning shipped JavaScript for network APIs. Because a walk that finds nothing proves nothing, four self-tests feed the walker synthetic React, fetch, site-path, remote-import, directive and import-time-DOM-global files and assert it reports each, and a coverage assertion fails if the walk never reached the tool modules. engine.test.ts loads the entry in Node with no DOM globals and runs real operations. README.md records what still blocks a CLI or MCP server against this tree: no package entry or build step, no process boundary, no ONNX inference because onnxruntime-web fetches its own assets, JPEG re-encoding needs a browser canvas, and canvas drawing stays in the site. Not merged, not pushed. package.json's format script does not cover engine/, so oxfmt does not check it; extending that glob needs a board request.

Owner decision 15. A record a person can download after a job, built only from measured facts: route pathname, tool id, version and execution mode from the build-time manifest, operation name, the duration the tool reported, requests the page started during the job by origin and initiator type, loads the CSP blocked by directive and origin, and the policy this build is configured to send for that route. No file name, size or hash, and no full URLs, paths or query strings, because those can carry user data. Every fact states how it was obtained and admits when it could not be: explicit measured, complete, blockedAttemptsMeasured and blockedAttemptsComplete flags mean a browser without Resource Timing yields 'not measured' rather than a zero. The limitations are part of the document, including that it cannot see extensions, other tabs, the OS or other devices, that worker requests live in the worker's own timeline, that the policy shown is the configured one rather than the received headers, and that it is not proof no data left the device and not an audit opinion. Capture is one call at the end of announceCompletion before any listener runs. Not reachable in the UI yet: components/completion-value-dialog.tsx belongs to Antigravity, so the button ships standalone and mounting it needs a board request. Not merged, not pushed.

The accompanying playbook targets 50 dollars a day on an asymmetry: one-off tips at three dollars need about seventeen every day, which at any plausible tip rate on a free utility means hundreds of thousands of completed tasks a month and scales with traffic, while recurring at five dollars a month needs three hundred members and scales with audience. Recurring is therefore the floor and tips the upside. Two existing assets are being wasted: milestone-modal.tsx already counts completed tasks locally and fires at fifty uses, the strongest membership moment the product has, and spends it on a generic link; and the completion dialog discards the per-job facts announceCompletion measures. Reverted from main on the owner's instruction so the other three merged branches could ship green. The processing record failed e2e in WebKit at a roughly 50 percent rate: --repeat-each=6 gave 3 failed and 3 passed, and a passing run recorded requestsDuringJob 1 correctly, so this was never a deterministic bug and my first report calling it reproducible was wrong. The cause is a limit in what the measurement can promise rather than a coding slip. A Resource Timing entry is only created when a load completes, but the record's declared window is requests started during the job. The single page request in this job is the PDF worker script and the job lasts about 29ms, so when that load has not finished at snapshot time no entry exists and the request is invisible; the record then reports requestsDuringJob 0 for a job that did make a request. The complete flag does not catch it because it is derived only from resource-timing buffer overflow, never from requests still in flight, so the record can state measured true, complete true and a count of zero while being wrong. On a product whose pitch is that nothing leaves the device, a confident zero is the most load-bearing claim it could get wrong, which is why this was not shipped and not papered over by relaxing the assertion. The test is correct to demand the record match observed reality; that agreement is the feature. Nothing was discarded: the work remains on branch claude/attestation and is recoverable, and the original ledger entry for building it is left in place because this file is append-only. Fixing it means changing the measurement contract, either collecting entries that arrive after the window through a PerformanceObserver and deferring the snapshot, or stating plainly that loads in flight at measurement time are not counted and setting complete false. Also noted for whoever picks it up: lib/attestation/network.ts carried two raw NUL bytes used as composite map-key separators, written as literal bytes instead of a unicode escape, which is why git recorded it as binary and plain grep refused to match it.
